title: F Flips to V
kidRule: Some words that end in F or FE change the F to V and add ES when there is more than one: shelf becomes shelves and knife becomes knives. Not all of them do, though: roofs and chefs just add S.
hint: Say the word for just one, then say it for many. Listen closely: did the last sound change from a soft blow to a buzz?
reminder: For these words, change the F to V and add E-S.

check.question: Why is there a V in SHELVES when SHELF ends in F?
check.correctAnswer: In some words, F changes to V before we add ES to mean more than one!
distractors: Because the letter L always turns F into V
Because F is never allowed in the middle of a word

words.def: Flat boards on a wall or in a cupboard where you keep things.
words.sent: The library shelves were full of books.
words.story: The biggest library in the world, in Washington, D.C., has more than 800 miles of shelves!
words.card: The *elves* stacked cookies on all the *shelves*!

words.def: Tools with sharp edges that are used for cutting food.
words.sent: Dad keeps the kitchen knives in a high drawer.
words.story: A table set for a fancy dinner has different knives for different jobs, even a small blunt one just for butter!
words.card: F*ive* butter *knives* lined up to d*ive* into the jam!

words.def: Small make-believe people with pointed ears.
words.sent: The elves made toys all night long.
words.story: In Iceland, a few roads have been built to curve around rocks where people say elves live!
words.card: *El*even *elves* rode an *el*ephant to the toy shop!

words.def: Whole breads, baked in one piece before being sliced.
words.sent: The baker pulled six warm loaves from the oven.
words.story: Burnt loaves of bread almost 2,000 years old were found still inside an oven in the ancient city of Pompeii!
words.card: The g*oa*t balanced three *loaves* on his horns!

words.def: A word for the same people or animals you were just talking about.
words.sent: The kittens washed themselves after lunch.
words.story: Only a few animals, like elephants, dolphins, and great apes, seem to know that the animal in a mirror is really themselves!
words.card: I told *them* to behave, but the socks tied *themselves* in knots!

words.def: The two equal parts you get when you cut something down the middle.
words.sent: We cut the sandwich into two halves.
words.story: Your brain has two halves, and the left one controls the right side of your body!

words.def: Long pieces of cloth worn around your neck to keep warm.
words.sent: We wore hats and scarves in the snow.
words.story: A man in Norway spent about thirty years knitting one scarf that ended up nearly three miles long!
words.card: The snowman drove a *car* full of stripy *scarves*!

words.def: The hard feet of animals like horses, cows, and goats.
words.sent: We heard the clip-clop of hooves on the road.
words.story: Hooves are made of the same stuff as your fingernails!
words.card: '*Hoo*, *hoo*!' said the owl, tapping the pony's *hooves*!

words.def: Baby cows, or the babies of whales and elephants.
words.sent: Two calves followed their mother across the meadow.
words.story: Giraffe calves can stand up and walk within about an hour of being born!
words.card: The *calves* checked the *cal*endar to see when the grass party began!

words.sent: The thieves were caught with the stolen cookies.
words.story: Raccoons look like little masked thieves, and their clever paws really can open jars and latches!
words.card: '*Hi*!' said the *thieves*, forgetting they were supposed to be sneaky!
